result.summary: Optimizes `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` in the libbitcoinkernel C API from O(n) to O(1) by pre-parsing and caching spans to witness items in `btck_WitnessStack`. Changes `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` to return a newly allocated, owned `btck_WitnessStack*` handle rather than an unowned pointer, and removes the C++ wrapper's `WitnessStackView` in favor of returning an owned `WitnessStack`.
result.problem: Since #36895 changed `CScriptWitness` to store witness stacks in serialized form, `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` scans from the start of the serialized data on each call, resulting in O(n^2) runtime when consumers read all items in a witness stack.
evidence: PR description: 'Since #36895, `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` walks the items before the one it returns, so reading a whole witness stack through it is O(n^2).'
result.scope_notes: Contains breaking changes to libbitcoinkernel's C and C++ APIs: `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` returns an allocated handle requiring `btck_witness_stack_destroy`, and `WitnessStackView` is removed from the C++ wrapper.
result.changed_since_previous: Replaced the previous approach of introducing a new `btck_witness_stack_get_items` bulk retrieval function. Instead, `btck_WitnessStack` now parses and caches spans for each item on creation, making `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` O(1) and changing `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` to return an owned handle.
result.card: Makes btck_witness_stack_get_item_at O(1) in libbitcoinkernel by pre-parsing item spans into btck_WitnessStack. After serialized witness storage was introduced in #36895, accessing witness items sequentially required scanning from the beginning each time, yielding O(n^2) total traversal time. This change eliminates the quadratic bottleneck while introducing a breaking C/C++ API change: btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack now returns an owned handle that callers must destroy, and WitnessStackView is dropped.

risk.why: Alters memory ownership semantics in the public C/C++ kernel API; incorrect handle destruction or lifetime mismanagement could cause memory leaks or crashes in external callers.
